brackets.section: Departmental Notice #1, "For 2026, the state adjusted gross income tax rate for individuals is 2.95%"
brackets.note: Flat 2.95% for 2026, one schedule for all filing statuses. The DOR rates page says the rate adjusts to 2.90% in 2027. Tax Foundation and PolicyEngine agree.

earnedIncomeCredit.note: "ten percent (10%) of the amount of the federal earned income tax credit" under section 32 "as in effect on January 1, 2023", with the federal cost of living adjustments applied, refundable. Section 32 has not changed since that date, so this is 10% of the actual federal credit, which is what the 2025 IT-40 booklet says.
earnedIncomeCredit.name: Indiana earned income credit

personalExemption.section: Departmental Notice #1, Tables A and B
personalExemption.note: $1,000 per exemption for the filer, spouse and each dependent, and an additional $1,500 for each qualifying dependent child, both read in the notice. The dependent figure here is $2,500, which is $1,000 plus the $1,500 additional exemption, on the assumption that the dependent is a qualifying child. A dependent who is not a qualifying child gets $1,000. Tax Foundation lists $1,000 per dependent and puts the extra $1,500 in its footnote (w). PolicyEngine has the same two amounts.

rules.note: Local tax flag is from Departmental Notice #1 (county rate table). Contribution flags checked on 2026-11-12 against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 (oracle/flags.py), which moves this state's tax by the same amount as this engine for 401k, HSA, IRA and health premium contributions. FSA and commuter benefits are not PolicyEngine inputs and rest on the state starting from federal income. Not read in the state's own instructions. No employee payroll contribution: the US Department of Labor's comparison lists worker unemployment contributions only in Alaska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania and disability insurance only in California, Hawaii, New Jersey, New York and Rhode Island, and no paid leave or similar program with an employee contribution was found for this state on 2026-11-12.
notes: Indiana counties levy their own income tax, based on the county of residence (or of principal work for nonresidents) on January 1. County rates in Departmental Notice #1 run from about 0.5% to 3%, applied to the same income after exemptions as the state tax. Not modeled.
Indiana has no standard deduction. Tax is a flat rate on federal AGI, with Indiana modifications, less exemptions.
Not modeled: other exemptions in Departmental Notice #1, namely an extra $1,500 for a first-time dependent, $3,000 for an adopted child, and additional exemptions for filers 65 or older or blind.
Not modeled: Indiana deductions such as the renter's deduction, and credits such as the unified tax credit for the elderly.
